scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that classroom technology can distract, then argues it also greatly aids learning; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Screens are now part of almost every classroom around the world.
Some people argue that technologies like video, computers, and the internet too often distract students from real learning.
I agree that these tools can distract, but I believe they also help learning greatly when they are used well.
First, it is true that classroom technology can easily distract students.
A device meant for study can quickly become a doorway to games, videos, and social media.
For example, a student with a laptop may drift into browsing instead of following the lesson.
This shows that technology can pull attention away from the very learning it was meant to support.
Endless notifications and entertainment make deep concentration harder than ever.
Used carelessly, these tools can leave students busy but learning very little.
To this extent, the warning in the statement is well founded.
Second, however, these same technologies can powerfully support real learning.
The internet gives students instant access to information that once took days to find.
Consider how a video can make a difficult idea clear in minutes, or how online lessons reach distant students.
Such tools show that technology can open doors to learning that were once firmly shut.
Computers also let students practise, explore, and learn at their own pace.
The problem lies not in the tools themselves but in how carelessly they are sometimes used.
Technology, then, can either harm or help, depending entirely on how it is handled.
In conclusion, classroom technology can indeed distract students from real learning.
But the same tools can deepen and widen learning when they are used with care.
Whether technology helps or harms depends far less on the tools than on how wisely we use them.
